channel.title: Cadence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: Remote Therapeutic Monitoring at a Turning Point
item.description: Proposed changes in the 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule could significantly limit physical therapy practices' ability to provide Remote Therapeutic Monitoring (RTM) through contracted clinical support models in the US.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Advancing Payment: What the Proposed 2027 Medicare Fee Schedule Means for PTs
item.description: APTA has released an analysis of the proposed 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule, highlighting key provisions affecting physical therapists' payment and practice, with a call for member comments by Sept. 14.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Modest Payment Increases Finalized by CMS for SNFs and IRFs
item.description: CMS finalized modest payment increases for Skilled Nursing Facilities (SNFs) and Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities (IRFs) for fiscal year 2027, while introducing earlier deadlines for care initiation and interdisciplinary team meetings for IRFs, and requiring all-payer Minimum Data Set submissions for SNFs starting October 1.
item.author: APTA

item.title: Carrying an unseen weight: the neuro-perceptual landscape of limb heaviness after stroke- a scoping review.
item.description: A scoping review identified perceived limb heaviness as an under-recognized stroke symptom, often unrelated to weakness or spasticity. Proposed mechanisms include altered sensorimotor integration, impaired proprioception, and disrupted body representation, suggesting issues in sensorimotor processing.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: White Matter Diffusion Anisotropy and the Effects of Inpatient Multidisciplinary Rehabilitation in Parkinson's Disease: A Diffusion Tensor Imaging Analysis.
item.description: A diffusion tensor imaging analysis found that pretreatment corticospinal tract fractional anisotropy predicted responsiveness to an 8-week inpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation program in 94 Parkinson's disease patients, with responders showing significant UPDRS Part III improvement.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Aquatic Tai Chi and Computer Assisted Rehabilitation Environment-Based Virtual Reality Training on Rehabilitation in Patients with Parkinson Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: A single-blind RCT with 50 Parkinson's disease patients (Hoehn-Yahr stage 2-3) compared 12 weeks of aquatic Tai Chi (n=26) versus Computer Assisted Rehabilitation Environment-based virtual reality training (n=24). Both interventions led to improvements in UPDRS-III, BBS, TUG, and 6-minute walk test.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in the emergency department (RESHAP-ED): a randomised controlled trial with economic evaluation.
item.description: The RESHAP-ED pragmatic RCT evaluated physiotherapist-led care for musculoskeletal conditions in five Australian emergency departments, demonstrating improved effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness compared to usual care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Focal Muscle Vibration for Upper Limb Spasticity After Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies (inception-March 2026) involving adults with post-stroke upper limb spasticity found focal muscle vibration (FMV) has a significant effect (Hedges' g=0.74, 95% CI 0.52-0.97) on reducing spasticity.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: The Optimal Exercise Modality and Dose for Blood Pressure Management in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Systematic Review with Bayesian Model-Based, and Dose-Response Network Meta-Analysis of RCTs.
item.description: This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis of RCTs identified optimal exercise modalities and doses for lowering resting systolic and diastolic BP in middle-aged and older adults (≥45 years) by May 2025.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Biofeedback in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review with meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analysis of randomized trials found that adding biofeedback to practice effectively improves lower limb activity in people with Parkinson's disease compared to practice alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Application of non-invasive electroencephalogram-based brain-computer interfaces in post-stroke hand function rehabilitation.
item.description: This article reviews the application of non-invasive EEG-based brain-computer interfaces (BCI) for post-stroke hand function rehabilitation. BCI decodes imagined hand movements to drive exoskeletons, FES, or VR devices, aiming to remodel neural pathways and promote motor recovery.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Development and psychometric validation of the shoulder problems assessment scale.
item.description: This multicenter study developed and validated the 12-item Shoulder Problems Assessment Scale (SPAS), an activity-based patient-reported outcome measure using a hierarchical stepwise yes/no format, with field testing on n = 415 patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Arm exercise training in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
item.description: This umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses synthesizes findings on arm exercise training in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), screening six databases up to May 2026.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Prestroke Rehabilitation Reserve and Mobility and Self-Care Outcomes After Incident Stroke Across Four International Aging Cohorts.
item.description: A harmonized longitudinal cohort study (N=7486, mean age 70.0 years) across four international aging cohorts found that lower multidimensional pre-stroke rehabilitation reserve was associated with adverse mobility and self-care status after incident stroke.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparison of high-intensity laser therapy and extracorporeal shock wave therapy for the treatment of plantar flexor spasticity in post-stroke patients.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial with 42 stroke patients compared high-intensity laser therapy (HILT) and radial extracorporeal shock wave therapy (rESWT) as adjunctive treatments for plantar flexor spasticity, with both groups showing greater improvements than rehabilitation alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A grade-specific clinical prediction rule for independent walking after traumatic spinal cord injury.
item.description: A clinical prediction rule was developed using the National Spinal Cord Injury Statistical Centre dataset (2607 patients) to predict independent walking one year after traumatic spinal cord injury, with differentiated prognoses for individual ASIA Impairment Scale grades.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Characteristics of Outpatient Care Settings Associated with Implementation Outcomes for a Group Physical Therapy Program.
item.description: A secondary analysis of a cluster randomized hybrid implementation trial identified organizational and contextual characteristics associated with the successful adoption and implementation of group physical therapy for knee osteoarthritis in 19 VHA outpatient PT departments.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Operational AI Adoption in U.S. Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities: Organizational Selection and Domain Heterogeneity, 2021-2024
item.description: U.S. Inpatient Rehabilitation Facilities (IRFs) are increasingly adopting operational AI solutions between 2021 and 2024, driven by workforce shortages and the complex Medicare prospective payment system, with varied adoption across clinical domains.
item.author: Archives of PM&R

item.title: Reframing patient expectations as therapeutic targets in musculoskeletal care.
item.description: This professional practice article argues that patient expectations (PEs) are not merely prognostic indicators but modifiable, multidimensional therapeutic targets that extend beyond treatment and recovery to influence outcomes in musculoskeletal care.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Strengthening Cardiac Rehabilitation: Key Strategies for Enhancing Accessibility and Outcomes
item.description: A qualitative study interviewed 10 leaders from high-performing cardiac rehabilitation programs to identify strategies associated with improved patient participation and adherence. Findings reveal practical approaches to enhance accessibility and outcomes in CR.
item.author: medRxiv
